BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: BCG Report Projects Gaming Industry Revenues Will Hit $350 Billion by 2030 Cloud Gaming Revenue Will Reach $18.3 Billion by 2030, Up 57% from 2023 40% of Gamers Are Consuming More User-Generated Content Than Last Year BOSTON —The gaming industry is emerging from its post-pandemic slowdown, with global gaming revenue projected to grow by 6% from 2026 to 2030 and reach $350 billion by 2030.
A new survey of approximately 3,000 gamers found that 55% of them increased their playing time during the past six months.
UGC has emerged as a rapidly growing creator economy, with payouts that will reach $1.5 billion in 2025 from two games alone.
More than 40% of survey respondents said that they’re consuming more UGC this year than last year, but only 10% to 15% have created content themselves.
Although 60% of respondents said they had tried cloud gaming, and 80% reported a positive experience, only 27% of gamers said they are regular or heavy users of cloud gaming.
Still, cloud gaming revenues are set to grow from around $1.4 billion in 2025 to $18.3 billion in 2030, and the number of users will surpass 50 million.
BCG’s report estimates that mobile in-app purchases in 2025 will approach $130 billion, nearly half of global industry revenue.

records.evidence:
Our survey finds that most surveyed consumers (53%) are now either experimenting with gen AI or using it regularly—up sharply from 38% in 2024 (figure 1).
1 Overall, tech affordability pressures appear to be easing slightly.
Deloitte Insights and our research centers deliver proprietary research designed to help organizations turn their aspirations into action.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Our survey finds that most surveyed consumers (53%) are now either experimenting with gen AI or using it regularly—up sharply from 38% in 2024 (figure 1).
Gen AI users—those who use it regularly for projects and tasks beyond experimentation—nearly doubled to 20% over the past year.
Roughly half of surveyed gen AI users (51%) say they use it every day, and 38% say they use it at least once a week, which suggests that gen AI is becoming part of their routine digital activities.
Deloitte’s 2025 Connected Consumer survey shows that US households spent an average of US$896 on connected devices in the past year—a significant uptick from US$764 in 2024.
Looking ahead, 29% of respondents say they plan to boost their device spending in the coming year—up threefold from 2023—while 24% say they’re looking to cut back on their device spending (figure 3).
In 2025, about half of respondents (51%) say they expect affordability challenges in the coming year, compared to 61% of respondents in 2024.

Among surveyed consumers, 23% expect to delay device purchases, 17% anticipate not being able to afford the more advanced devices their household wants, and 16% think they may cut back on tech services, subscriptions, or software.
Respondents report that their households spend an average of US$183 monthly on digital services, a slight uptick from US$175 in 2024.

The data suggests this upward trend is likely to continue: A quarter of survey respondents expect to increase their spending on tech services and subscriptions—a sharp jump from 14% who said the same last year.
Another 57% of respondents say they plan to keep their spending steady, down significantly from 72% last year.

Personal use leads gen AI adoption, but work-related use is growing fast Personal use remains the leading application of gen AI, cited by 85% of surveyed users and experimenters, while 22% say they use it for educational or school purposes.
Work-related use (among employed respondents) shows steady growth, climbing from 6% in 2023 to 34% in 2025 (figure 4).
Among those surveyed who are using gen AI for work, more than half (55%) say their organizations encourage its use, and 40% say their companies provide training.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: 68% prioritise AI features in next smartphone, but 82% say trust will decide the purchase: Report AI has overtaken design, price and battery life in purchase priorities, while consumers increasingly demand transparent data practices and on-device AI processing.

A new study by CyberMedia Research (CMR) found that 68% of consumers now prioritise AI capabilities when evaluating smartphones, while 82% said transparent data practices are essential for trusting AI-powered experiences.
The study found that 61% of respondents believe on-device AI processing improves both responsiveness and privacy, indicating growing awareness of how AI functions on smartphones.
Performance remains the most important consideration for smartphone buyers, cited by 78% of respondents, followed by camera quality, including AI enhancements (70%), and AI features (59%).

When choosing between similarly priced devices, 60% of consumers said they prefer a smartphone that offers both strong AI capabilities and powerful hardware, while 25% described themselves as AI-first buyers.
The trend is particularly strong among younger consumers, with 72% of Gen Z respondents saying AI will influence their next smartphone purchase, compared with 65% of millennials.

AI-powered photography continues to be the most widely used application, with 77% of respondents regularly using features such as low-light enhancement, portrait optimisation and intelligent scene detection.
While 66% of female consumers primarily use AI for camera and imaging features, 42% of male respondents prioritise productivity and communication use cases.
CMR also referenced its India Mobile Handset Market Review Report, which found that MediaTek accounted for 47% of smartphone chipset shipments in India.
The survey additionally reported that 93% of MediaTek users expressed satisfaction with their devices, while more than 45% said they would prefer a MediaTek-powered smartphone.

records.evidence:
Valid responses totaled 10,000 for the screening survey and 3,300 for the main survey.
Its first survey, titled "Consumer AI Usage Survey 2026.7," examined how AI is being used in purchasing behavior and decision-making.
Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning

Dentsu Digital launches with AI Lab and publishes a July 2026 survey on consumer AI use in purchasing About one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and financial categories above 50% AI use is strongest in awareness, comparison and post-purchase stages, while final buying decisions remain more human-led Dentsu Digital said on July 23 that about one in three consumers who use artificial intelligence in their private lives had consulted AI about purchases made within the past six months, releasing the first findings from a new in-house research unit focused on consumer behavior in the AI era.

The ratio was highest in higher-involvement categories where consumers tend to compare options more closely, with 57% in travel planning and accommodation bookings and 56% in financial products and insurance.

Across product categories, 2% to 3% of respondents said they adopted AI responses as-is for their final decision, indicating that some consumers are beginning to leave the ultimate purchase choice to AI.

sourceLines: Valid responses totaled 10,000 for the screening survey and 3,300 for the main survey.
Its first survey, titled "Consumer AI Usage Survey 2026.7," examined how AI is being used in purchasing behavior and decision-making.
Dentsu Digital said the findings show AI use is spreading in awareness, comparison and post-purchase phases, while people still account for a higher share of decision-making at the final stage.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Only 45% of marketers gain quality from AI, WARC and TikTok find
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

According to the survey, 90% of marketers agree generative AI has become a key tool in the creative development process, 72% use it frequently as a regular part of content production, and 87% believe their organisation is using it effectively for creative development.
WARC's Marketer's Toolkit found that 59% of marketers agree traditional demographic segmentation is no longer effective.
Yet the new survey found demographic data remains the primary input used to brief AI, relied on by 67% of respondents.
Only 17% of marketers make it a rule to always incorporate community or audience insights beyond demographics into generative AI workflows.

Asked to identify the biggest gaps in inputs currently available when briefing generative AI, respondents pointed first to audience behavioural data covering how people engage rather than who they are, cited by 45%.
Access to real-time cultural or community signals and tools that translate insights into effective AI briefs each registered 35%.
Only 10% of respondents said they do not perceive significant gaps in the inputs available to them.

According to the survey, 86% of marketers agree audience behaviour and community signals will influence creative development significantly more over the next three years, and one in three believe access to richer audience or cultural signals would do most to unlock generative AI advantage.

A Taboola study across a publisher network of roughly 600 million daily active users found AI-generated creatives increased or maintained click-through rates without damaging conversion rates , with strongest results in food and drink and personal finance and more muted outcomes in categories such as education.
The WARC and TikTok figure of 87% of marketers believing their organisation uses generative AI effectively sits awkwardly against other industry measurement.
A MiQ survey from November 2025, reported by PPC Land , found 72% of marketers planning AI adoption growth while only 45% felt confident.
The same MIQ Global AI Confidence Curve is cited inside the WARC report itself for a separate finding: only 40% of marketers strongly believe they can apply findings from one campaign to another.
A self-reported 87% effectiveness rating from a vendor-commissioned survey and a 45% confidence rating from an independent one describe the same industry.
Brandwatch survey findings reported in April 2026 identified social listening and consumer research as a top skill gap at 55%, with cross-platform content optimisation at 52%.

records.evidence:
Omdia estimates that cellular standard devices, meaning smartphones using 4G or 5G technologies to connect directly to satellites, will become the dominant model in the smartphone satellite D2D market, accounting for over 95% of global total MAUs by 2030.
This represents mean annual growth rates of 80.1% for users and 49.4% for revenue from 2026 to 2030.
“In contrast to dual-mode phone solutions, which require a proprietary satellite communication link in the smartphone, cellular standard based solutions, such as Starlink D2C and AST SpaceMobile, can directly connect to devices compliant with 4G or 5G standards, particularly existing smartphones,” noted Guang Yang, Senior Principal Analyst, Service Provider Strategies and Mobile Infrastructure, at Omdia .

sourceLines: Omdia estimates that cellular standard devices, meaning smartphones using 4G or 5G technologies to connect directly to satellites, will become the dominant model in the smartphone satellite D2D market, accounting for over 95% of global total MAUs by 2030.
This represents mean annual growth rates of 80.1% for users and 49.4% for revenue from 2026 to 2030.

“In contrast to dual-mode phone solutions, which require a proprietary satellite communication link in the smartphone, cellular standard based solutions, such as Starlink D2C and AST SpaceMobile, can directly connect to devices compliant with 4G or 5G standards, particularly existing smartphones,” noted Guang Yang, Senior Principal Analyst, Service Provider Strategies and Mobile Infrastructure, at Omdia .

summaryLines: Omdia는 4G 또는 5G 기술을 사용하여 위성에 직접 연결하는 스마트폰을 의미하는 셀룰러 표준 장치가 스마트폰 위성 D2D 시장에서 지배적인 모델이 되어 2030년까지 전 세계 총 MAU의 95% 이상을 차지할 것으로 추정함
이는 2026년부터 2030년까지 사용자의 연평균 성장률은 80.1%, 매출의 경우 49.4%를 나타냄

Forecast: Consumer agentic AI will soar to $3.3tn in 2030 Marketing is operating in an age of abundance.
The study finds that total agent-facilitated consumer spending will triple from $944 billion (€827.7bn) this year to $3.35 trillion in 2030.

James McDonald, Director of Data, Intelligence & Forecasting, WARC, and author of the research, added: “This landmark study finds that agentic AI is already facilitating the path to purchase for many consumers, and will become deeply embedded over the coming years to influence $3.35 trillion in household expenditure by 2030.

US: The US will lead agentic AI spending at $1.1 trillion (31.9 per cent of the global total), driven by consumers already comfortable with digital commerce and brands with the resources to deploy agents at scale.

China: China will be the second-largest market at $505.8 billion (15.1 per cent of global spend), powered by high platform integration, government support, and consumers ready to embrace delegated commerce.
UK: The UK will capture 3.9 per cent of global agentic AI spending ($131.2 billion), driven by strong talent, major investments, and government backing for AI-led transformation.

AI agents will influence $62 billion in spending in 2026, advising on party ideas, drink pairings, and occasions.

Media & Publishing: At $73.3 billion, this category is already one of the most impacted by agentic AI.

Retail: will see agent-facilitated spending grow 218.7 per cent – from $62.7 billion in 2026 to $199.9 billion in 2030 driven by omnichannel shopping and AI comparison.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: De-identified Health Data Market Size To Exceed $20.79 Billion By 2035

The global De-identified Health Data Market is expected to witness significant expansion as healthcare organizations, life sciences companies, and technology providers increasingly rely on privacy-compliant healthcare data to accelerate innovation while safeguarding patient confidentiality. “According to a recent study by SNS Insider, the global De-identified Health Data Market size valued at USD 8.52 billion in 2025, is anticipated to grow to USD 20.79 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 9.32% over the 2026–2035 forecast period.” However, with the increasing volume of clinical data from healthcare institutions across the globe using digital healthcare platforms, EMR, laboratory databases, and connected healthcare technology, there is an increase in the need for innovation within healthcare that is leading institutions to embrace de-identified data which facilitates medical research, artificial intelligence innovation, healthcare planning, and pharmaceutical innovation.
By data category, clinical data accounted for approximately 20.6% of global market revenue in 2025, reflecting its central role in medical research, healthcare analytics , and evidence generation.

Across applications, clinical research and trials represented approximately 25.62% of total market revenue in 2025, supported by growing reliance on real-world health information to improve study design and accelerate research activities.

The North American market had 39.7% of the world market revenue in 2025 due to its sophisticated digitization of healthcare, high usage of electronic health records , regulatory frameworks, and investments made in healthcare analytics and life sciences research.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.
As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

“The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”
The study found that: Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

“If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”

이전에 보고된 바와 같이, 연구에 따르면 전 세계 장애 시장의 연간 소비 규모는 미화 13조 달러에 달해 세계 최대의 소비자 부문 중 하나임

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Gartner predicts AI models and platforms spend to hit US$64B - ARN

Worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms is projected to total US$64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from US$39 billion in 2025, with more and more enterprises are choosing to work with companies that can provide clear value.

Spending on generative AI (genAI) models is forecast to grow 117 per cent while AI platform spending will rise 36.9 per cent in 2026, according to Gartner’s latest forecast on AI platforms and models. “Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes ,” said the analyst firm’s senior principal research analyst, Arunasree Cheparthi. “Spending is shifting toward providers who can demonstrate clear value across cost, latency, performance, and reliability. “This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency, and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use.” However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use, and durable margins.
This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026.

According to Gartner, the AI software market is forecast to grow significantly between 2025 and 2026, with total market revenue increasing from US$39.3 billion to US$64.3 billion, representing 63.4 per cent growth.
The Foundation Generative AI Models segment is expected to more than double, rising from US$11.4 billion in 2025 to US$23.4 billion in 2026, representing a growth rate of 104.2 per cent.
Meanwhile, the fastest-growing segment is DSLMs and specialised genAI models, which is projected to expand from US$1.6 billion to US$4.9 billion, achieving 210.0 per cent growth.

AI application development platforms are forecast to grow from US$6.9 billion to US$9.5 billion (up 38.6 per cent), and AI platforms for data science and machine learning are expected to increase from US$19.4 billion to US$26.4 billion (an increase of 36.3 per cent).

Overall, these projections highlight accelerating investment in generative AI technologies, particularly in specialised AI and foundation models . “Over the long-term, the biggest winners will be vendors that help enterprises manage where and how AI is used across the business ,” said Cheparthi. “As more models enter the market and usage-based pricing becomes harder to predict, buyers will turn to platforms that help them choose the right tools, monitor performance , enforce policy and keep costs under control.” Equinix passes top Australian leadership to Jarrod Nink Cohesity promotes Peter Hanna to lead growth in Asia Pacific and Japan As White House monitors latest OpenAI incident, Congress eyes an AI ‘kill switch’ for DHS news EDGE 2026: Becoming the successful MSP for the future 28 Jul 2026 6 mins news EDGE 2026: The MSP of the future 27 Jul 2026 4 mins news AI data centre growth ignites debate over power, water, and infrastructure 27 Jul 2026 11 mins news Monvia lists on ASX after $17.5M IPO 24 Jul 2026 2 mins news SoftwareOne adds NinjaOne to portfolio 24 Jul 2026 2 mins news Adactin teams up with Cyara to support AI-powered customer service 23 Jul 2026 2 mins news Synnex strengthens Microsoft practice with four Microsoft specialisations 23 Jul 2026 3 mins news Datacom considers next steps for local MD role as Laura Malcolm departs 22 Jul 2026 3 mins Leading Edge DC hires Schneider Electric’s Joe Craparotta as CEO Ingram Micro Australia added to Oracle’s Cloud Distribution Program

${VOLUME} ${CHANGE} ${change_PERC}% Spending on generative AI models is expected to grow 117% in 2026, while AI platforms are forecasted to increase by 36.9% Worldwide end-user spending on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms and models is projected to reach $64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from $39 billion in 2025, according to a report by Gartner, a business and technology insights company.
It highlighted that spending on generative AI (GenAI) models is expected to grow 117 per cent in 2026, while spending on AI platforms is forecast to increase 36.9 per cent during the year.
According to the forecast, spending on Foundation Generative AI Models will increase from $11.4 billion in 2025 to $23.4 billion in 2026, registering a growth of 104.2 per cent.
Meanwhile, spending on DSLMs and Specialised GenAI Models is expected to rise from $1.6 billion to $4.9 billion, marking a 210 per cent increase in 2026.

The report also projected spending on AI Application Development Platforms to increase from $6.9 billion in 2025 to $9.5 billion in 2026, while spending on AI Platforms for Data Science and Machine Learning is expected to rise from $19.4 billion to $26.4 billion during the same period.

records.evidence:
Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.
Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered

Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
Mordor Intelligence sizes the global AI code tools market at roughly $9.35 billion in 2026, expanding at more than 26% a year.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.
Copilot Pro still lists at $10 a month and Copilot Enterprise at $39 per user per month, but both now sit on top of a metered layer that tracks actual usage rather than assuming it away.

GitHub’s own research previously found that Copilot users complete tasks about 55% faster than developers coding without it, a strong pitch for adoption but a rough one for margins once millions of developers start running agentic workflows against the same infrastructure.
A flat $20 monthly subscription only works if the average user’s token consumption stays well below what that fee actually covers.
That behaviour is a major reason Claude Code was reported to author close to 4% of all public GitHub commits by early 2026, a figure some analysts expect to pass 20% before the year is out.
The spread between roughly $9 billion and $34 billion for the same year comes down to scope.

Taking the narrower, more comparable estimates from Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, and Research and Markets, the market sits close to $9 to $10 billion in 2026 and is on track for somewhere between $19 billion and $26 billion by 2030.

Surveys circulating in early 2026 put Claude Code’s “most loved” rating among senior engineers at 46%, against 19% for Cursor and 9% for GitHub Copilot, and separate JetBrains-linked data credits Claude Code with a 91% customer satisfaction score and a net promoter score of 54, the highest reported in the category.

In startups under 50 employees, Claude Code adoption reportedly reaches 75% against 42% for Cursor, while GitHub Copilot holds a commanding 56% share inside companies with more than 10,000 employees, largely on the back of existing Microsoft procurement relationships.
Copilot’s installed base remains enormous regardless, with more than 15 million developers across upwards of 77,000 organisations, including a reported 77% of the Fortune 500.

엔터프라이즈 소프트웨어는 2010년대에 영구 라이센스에서 사용자당 SaaS 구독으로 전환함 · 이는 일회성 판매보다 사용량을 더 자세히 추적하는 수익이 필요한 공급업체에 의해 주도된 또 다른 변화임
GitHub는 Copilot을 사용량 기반 청구로 전환하여 계획에 포함된 허용량이 소진되면 프리미엄 요청에 대해 현재 일정에 따라 요청당 약 $0.04의 요금으로 청구함

summaryLinesEn: Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.

Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

records.title: 60% of agentic AI costs go to response refinement, and most enterprises are already over budget
records.titleEn: 60% of agentic AI costs go to response refinement, and most enterprises are already over budget

values.label: 응답 비중 · 2026
values.sourceLine: McKinsey's Enterprise AI FinOps Survey, conducted in May 2026 with 75 qualified respondents across five major industries, found that 93 percent have already blown past their AI budgets.

values.label: 비율
values.sourceLine: If 60 percent of the bill sits in refinement loops rather than primary inference, and most budget frameworks were built around inference costs alone, the gap between forecast and actual spend will widen as agentic deployments scale.

values.label: 비용·소득 영향액 · 2024
values.sourceLine: Inference on GPT-3.5-level capability cost $20 per million tokens in early 2024 and fell to $0.07 by year's end, according to the Stanford HAI 2025 AI Index cited in McKinsey's new report.

Alphabet's first-ever negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion masked Google Cloud's 82% revenue surge to $24.8 billion with operating margins tripling.
A record $514 billion signed cloud backlog means much of Alphabet's $205 billion capex is effectively pre-sold before the infrastructure even goes live.
Free cash flow came in at negative $5.9 billion, a stunning reversal driven by an unprecedented surge in AI infrastructure spending.
Capital expenditures totaled $44.9 billion during the quarter, doubling from a year ago.
Even more surprising, management raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $205 billion, signaling that spending is still accelerating rather than slowing.
Collectively, the industry’s largest AI builders are on pace to spend well over $700 billion in 2026.
Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% year over year to $24.8 billion.
Perhaps the most overlooked figure was Google’s $514 billion cloud backlog — signed customer contracts that haven’t yet been recognized as revenue.
Wall Street currently forecasts 23% revenue growth this year followed by 21% next year.
If Alphabet maintains roughly 20% annual growth into 2028, the company would exit that year generating approximately $2 billion in revenue every single day.

According to Alphabet’s earnings, Google is already converting AI investment into accelerating cloud revenue, expanding margins, and posting a record $514 billion backlog waiting to become future sales.

But if Alphabet continues executing at its current pace, today’s $205 billion investment program may eventually look less like reckless spending and more like the foundation of its next long-term competitive moat.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Matt Murphy: Inside the $500M Anthropic SPV That Changed Menlo Ventures — BigGo Finance
In early 2024, Matt Murphy walked into a meeting at Anthropic — a pre-revenue AI lab valued north of $4 billion, run by a team that hadn't yet launched a commercial model.
The deal was structurally awkward for Menlo Ventures, a firm that manages roughly $600 million per fund.
That $10 million starter check and the $500 million-plus SPV that followed would become the defining bet of his career.
The SPV itself was Menlo's first, raising over $500 million from limited partners and strategic investors in a process Murphy describes as the single hardest part of the entire deal.
"Never done before, over $500 million, first time," he said.

In applications where user experience directly drives business outcomes — where a 5% improvement in model quality translates to measurable gains in retention and revenue — companies will pay the premium.
Murphy frames it as an inevitable optimization for companies approaching $100 billion in revenue.
Lovable, an AI-first no-code app builder, rocketed from zero to $300 million in annual recurring revenue in roughly a year.
On one end: seed-stage "tracker checks" of $100,000 to $1 million into more than 50 companies per fund.
On the other end: concentrated, later-stage bets above $10 million in ARR, where a company has already emerged as a category leader.
"You're better off being in them at a very small percent than owning a large percent of a company that exits for $300 to $500 million," Murphy said.
Menlo's $3 billion in total fund commitments is calibrated to stay competitive: large enough to write lead checks, small enough to maintain cultural cohesion.

Moonshot's valuation had already increased from $4.3 billion in December to $20 billion within five months, supported by investors including IDG Capital, Alibaba, Meituan, a Chinese food-delivery and local-services company, and several major Chinese state funds.
For investors, Moonshot's recovery could strengthen interest in China's open-source AI sector, while its rapid valuation growth and rising revenue expectations may intensify comparisons with DeepSeek and other Chinese developers competing with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Following the Kimi K3 release, Moonshot's daily sales rose by at least six times, forcing the company to temporarily stop accepting new subscriptions because of limited computing capacity.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Moonshot Nears $30 Billion Valuation After Kimi K3 Release

/ Moonshot Nears $30 Billion Valuation After Kimi K3 Release Moonshot, a Chinese artificial intelligence startup behind the Kimi chatbot, has returned to the center of the global AI race after releasing Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion-parameter model that attracted intense attention at the World AI Conference.
The startup is finalizing a funding round that would value it at more than $30 billion and is considering a Hong Kong public listing in as soon as six months.

Moonshot's valuation had already increased from $4.3 billion in December to $20 billion within five months, supported by investors including IDG Capital, Alibaba, Meituan, a Chinese food-delivery and local-services company, and several major Chinese state funds.
These products helped lift annual recurring revenue above $100 million in March 2026, $200 million in April and $300 million in June, according to people familiar with the figures.

localization.title: Moonshot, Kimi K3 출시 후 300억 달러 가치 평가
summaryLines: Moonshot의 가치는 IDG Capital, Alibaba, 중국 음식 배달 및 지역 서비스 회사인 Meituan 및 여러 주요 중국 국영 기금을 포함한 투자자의 지원을 받아 이미 12월 43억 달러에서 5개월 만에 200억 달러로 증가함
투자자들에게 Moonshot의 회복은 중국의 오픈 소스 AI 부문에 대한 관심을 강화할 수 있는 반면, Moonshot의 빠른 가치 평가 성장과 매출 기대치 상승은 OpenAI 및 Anthropic과 경쟁하는 DeepSeek 및 기타 중국 개발자와의 비교를 강화할 수 있음
Kimi K3 출시 이후 Moonshot의 일일 판매량은 최소 6배 증가했으며, 제한된 컴퓨팅 용량으로 인해 회사는 일시적으로 신규 구독 수락을 중단함

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: IT Services Market Size To Exceed $3.35 Trillion By 2035

The global IT Services Market is entering a new phase of expansion as organizations across industries modernize technology ecosystems to improve operational efficiency, strengthen cyber resilience, and accelerate digital innovation. “According to a recent study by SNS Insider, the IT Services Market size valued at USD 1.50 trillion in 2025, is anticipated to grow to USD 3.35 trillion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 8.35% over the 2026–2035 forecast period.” With more companies turning towards the cloud, enterprise software, artificial intelligence, and connected infrastructure, the demand for managed and professional IT services is growing.

Key Market Insights Highlight Changing Enterprise Technology Priorities Based on type, Operations & Maintenance accounted for approximately 54.1% of market revenue in 2025 due to the continuous need for infrastructure support, application maintenance, and performance optimization.
By approach, Proactive IT Services represented around 58.5% of total revenue in 2025 owing to growing adoption of preventive monitoring and predictive maintenance strategies.
In terms of application, Systems & Network Management held nearly 47.8% market share in 2025 as businesses prioritize uninterrupted IT operations across hybrid infrastructure environments.

North America Held 36.5% of the IT Services Market Share in 2025; Asia Pacific Projected to Register the Fastest CAGR Through 2035 In 2025, the North American market is projected to account for around 36.5% of the global market revenue, largely due to high enterprise technology spending and cloud adoption, managed services, and cybersecurity investments across sectors.

records.evidence:
By the first half of 2025, close to 8,000 games had filed an AI disclosure on Steam, up from roughly 1,000 across all of 2024, an eightfold jump in about eighteen months.
The jump from roughly 1,000 disclosed games in 2024 to 8,000 by the first half of 2025 shows how fast generative tools moved from novelty to normal practice in PC game development.
A studio leaning on an AI coding assistant to speed up development does not need to say so on its store page.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Central Nervous System Therapeutic Market Size to Hit USD 285.72 Billion by 2035

The global central nervous system therapeutics market size accounted for USD 127.29 billion in 2025 and is predicted to increase from USD 138.62 billion in 2026 to approximately USD 285.72 billion by 2025, growing at a CAGR of 8.64% from 2026 to 2035.
North America dominated the market with the largest market share of 45 % in 2025.
By disease, the neurodegenerative diseases segment contributed more than 40% of the market share in 2025.

According to the World Health Organization, the central nervous system diseases such as Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, epilepsy, stroke, and multiple sclerosis affects around 1 billion people across the globe.
As per the Alzheimer's Association, over 5million people are affected with the Alzheimer's diseases and this number is projected to reach 14 million by 2050.
The soaring incidence of CNS disorders like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, epilepsy, stroke, and multiple sclerosis is having adverse effects on almost 1 billion individuals worldwide.
The neurodegenerative diseases segment accounted for a market share of around 40% and dominated the global central nervous system therapeutic market in 2025.

Ode has secured $1.5 billion in funding to deploy top-tier engineers for AI integration in businesses.

records.evidence:
The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.
While 61% have redesigned roles to support AI adoption and 24% are creating new AI-focused management positions, only one-third have fully implemented employee training programs focused on working alongside AI tools.
Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: The deployment of AI technology in enterprises has reached 57%, yet only 11% have achieved their primary objectives according to Kyndryl's 2026 People Readiness Report.
Fifty-seven percent of enterprises now have AI embedded in core business processes or deployed broadly across their organizations, up from 35% just one year ago.
Worldwide AI spending is forecast to reach $2.52 trillion in 2026, a 44% year-over-year increase, according to Gartner research cited in Kyndryl's report.

The Achievers Workforce Institute 's seventh annual State of Recognition Report, cited by MarketScale, found that just 19% of workers feel confident using AI tools, and only 18% feel supported in adapting to them.
Kyndryl's report isolates a cohort it calls Pacesetters: roughly 9% of respondents that are generating measurable AI returns.

While 61% have redesigned roles to support AI adoption and 24% are creating new AI-focused management positions, only one-third have fully implemented employee training programs focused on working alongside AI tools.
Kyndryl's data shows 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful business decisions within the next year.
Half of leaders surveyed, 52%, say it has become more challenging to find employees with the right skills to advance their AI strategy, according to the Kyndryl report.

Pressure-test your agentic AI plans against your current oversight model: 81% of organizations expect AI agents to make impactful decisions within a year, but only 25% fully trust AI without human oversight, making oversight architecture a critical gap to close before autonomous systems go live.

Rambus（RMBS）delivered a landmark quarter, shattering the $200 million revenue ceiling for the first time in its history.

The chip interface and IP specialist reported second-quarter revenue of $207.4 million, a 20% jump from a year ago and 15% higher than the previous quarter, driven by an insatiable appetite for faster memory in AI data centers and the accelerating shift to DDR5 technology.
Product revenue, the company's main growth engine, surged 22% year-over-year to $99.2 million.
Non-GAAP net income climbed to $84.4 million, translating to earnings of $0.77 per share, a 24% improvement over the prior-year period.
Cash generation remained robust, with operating cash flow of $61 million and free cash flow of $49 million.
Rambus ended the quarter with a fortified balance sheet, holding $825 million in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities.
In a deliberate move to navigate persistent supply chain tightness, Rambus increased its inventory by $16 million during the quarter.
The Silicon IP business remains a steady growth pillar, with management projecting an annual expansion rate of 10% to 15%.

For the third quarter, Rambus guided for revenue between $210 million and $216 million, with product revenue expected to land between $110 million and $116 million, representing a sequential increase of roughly 14% at the midpoint.
Non-GAAP earnings per share are forecast in the range of $0.75 to $0.82.
Rambus maintained its long-term product gross margin target of 60% to 65%, though quarterly fluctuations are expected due to product mix shifts and ongoing supply constraints.

records.evidence:
Total revenue reached $28.24 billion, up 26% year-over-year and surpassing the $25.71 billion average analyst estimate surveyed by LSEG.
Despite financial pressures, Tesla's core auto sales business showed strong recovery momentum in the second quarter.
Even as vehicle deliveries hit a record high and drove substantial revenue growth, the company burned through nearly $5.8 billion in just 90 days—sacrificing profits and cash flow to build the massive infrastructure needed to support artificial intelligence and humanoid robots.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Tesla Posts Record Q2 Revenue But Swings to Loss, Burns $5.8 Billion in 90 Days Betting on AI and Humanoid Robot Infrastructure — BigGo Finance

Even as vehicle deliveries hit a record high and drove substantial revenue growth, the company burned through nearly $5.8 billion in just 90 days—sacrificing profits and cash flow to build the massive infrastructure needed to support artificial intelligence and humanoid robots.
Following the release, Tesla shares fell more than 3% in after-hours trading as earnings missed expectations and free cash flow turned negative.
Total revenue reached $28.24 billion, up 26% year-over-year and surpassing the $25.71 billion average analyst estimate surveyed by LSEG.

The revenue growth was primarily driven by a strong rebound in global deliveries, with Tesla handing over more than 480,000 pure electric vehicles worldwide during the quarter—a roughly 25% year-over-year increase and a new all-time high.
Net income attributable to common shareholders was $1.114 billion, down 5% from $1.172 billion in the same period last year.
More concerning for investors, adjusted earnings per share came in at just $0.33, significantly below the average analyst estimate of $0.51.
Meanwhile, global carbon credit revenue plummeted to $146 million from $439 million in the prior-year quarter, further weighing on profitability.
In the second quarter, Tesla's capex reached $5.789 billion, surging 142% year-over-year.
By this measure, Tesla spent roughly $64.32 million per day over the past 90 days.
The massive outlay directly resulted in negative free cash flow of $1.092 billion—the first such occurrence in more than two years.
Musk has raised this year's capital expenditure forecast to over $25 billion, nearly triple last year's $8.5 billion.
Notably, actual spending in the first half reached $8.3 billion, meaning nearly $17 billion must be spent in the second half to fulfill the commitment.
Total automotive revenue for the period was $20.516 billion, up 23% year-over-year.
Among these, combined deliveries of the Model 3 and Model Y reached 467,762 units, a 25% increase, remaining the absolute workhorses.
The Model Y has held the title of the world's best-selling vehicle for three consecutive years, with cumulative sales now exceeding 4 million units.
First-half deliveries totaled nearly 468,000 units, up 28.4% year-over-year.
In Europe, the Model Y became the best-selling pure electric model in May with monthly sales exceeding 17,000 units.

In the Asia-Pacific market, Model Y sales in Australia skyrocketed 133.5% year-over-year, making it the best-selling vehicle across all categories in the local market for the second consecutive month.
In the robotaxi space, the Cybercab—a fully autonomous electric vehicle—has entered production at the Texas Gigafactory, with a designed annual capacity exceeding 125,000 units.

With the official retirement of the Model S and Model X production lines at the Fremont factory, the vacated space has begun installing Optimus's first-generation production line, with a planned annual capacity of 1 million units.
Meanwhile, a second production line at the Texas Gigafactory is already in preparation, with a long-term designed annual capacity of up to 10 million units.
On the assisted driving software front, FSD's global paid subscriber base has reached 1.48 million, with over half of new vehicles delivered in the North American market subscribing to the service.

As nearly $17 billion in second-half capital expenditure plans gradually materialize, the market will be watching closely to see whether this enormous investment can truly fortify its physical-world AI moat.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Enterprise AI Adoption: 59% Spend $1M+, 29% See ROI [2026] - tech-insider.org

Canadian businesses more than tripled their use of artificial intelligence in two years, moving from 6.1% adoption in the second quarter of 2024 to 19.2% by the same period in 2026, according to Statistics Canada.
Globally the pattern looks even sharper: 59% of organizations now spend at least $1 million a year on AI, based on a WRITER-commissioned survey of 2,400 executives and employees published in 2026.

The Productivity Paradox: 5x Personal Gains, 29% Company ROI Canada vs. the United States: A Smaller, Slower ROI Curve Market Impact: What the ROI Gap Means for Vendors and Buyers Competitive Comparison: How OpenAI, Microsoft, Google and Anthropic Are Responding What Comes Next: 5 Predictions for Enterprise AI Spending That gap between AI spending and AI payoff has become the defining budget fight inside technology departments this year.

Workplace Intelligence polled 2,400 people on WRITER’s behalf: 1,200 C-suite executives and 1,200 employees at companies ranging from 100 to more than 10,000 workers, spread across nearly 30 industries in the United States, United Kingdom, Ireland, the Benelux region, France, and Germany.
Fifty-nine percent of companies now invest $1 million or more annually in AI technology.

And in a finding that should worry any finance team, 54% of C-suite respondents said AI adoption is tearing their company apart internally, the product of fights over budget ownership, tool sprawl, and who decides which model powers which workflow.
The same WRITER research found that 67% of executives believe their company has already suffered a data breach tied to unapproved, employee-installed AI tools, a pattern often called shadow AI.
Seventy-nine percent of organizations now call AI a strategic priority, up from 74% in the first quarter, and 22% classify AI as simply part of everyday work, up from 13% the quarter before.
Average AI spending among surveyed organizations reached $188 million.
Despite that scale of investment, just 7% of organizations told KPMG they had established measurable ROI on their AI spending.

Twenty-four percent of organizations say they struggle specifically with managing usage-based AI costs, and 49% have already delayed or scaled back an AI initiative after its cost exceeded its measured value.
Companies with 100 or more employees report 27.8% adoption, compared with 19.9% among the smallest businesses.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate dropped 41 percent compared with 2024, though the region still posted the highest rate of any market DoubleVerify tracks, at 0.6 percent, driven mainly by the United States.
EMEA marketers instead prioritized the ability to review or approve AI-generated creatives, at 38 percent, ahead of data-privacy safeguards.
The company derives its wasted-spend estimates by multiplying total violations by an assumed cost per mille of 3 dollars, a figure the report applies uniformly across markets despite considerable variation in actual media pricing between, for instance, the United States and other markets in the same region.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

Reach out via luis@ppc.land LinkedIn DoubleVerify today released regional editions of its 2026 Global Insights report, "Media Quality in the Age of AI," reporting that fraud and invalid traffic violation rates fell 41 percent year over year in North America and 45 percent in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, while artificial intelligence bots generated up to ten times more clicks than humans in some unprotected ad campaigns.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate dropped 41 percent compared with 2024, though the region still posted the highest rate of any market DoubleVerify tracks, at 0.6 percent, driven mainly by the United States.
The Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate fell 45 percent year over year, continuing what DoubleVerify describes as the world's lowest regional rate for the metric.
Non-human data center traffic, the most prevalent fraud type in the region, dropped 54 percent.

Unprotected campaigns, meaning those without DoubleVerify's pre-bid or post-bid safeguards, recorded a fraud violation rate of 2.8 percent globally, compared with 0.6 percent for protected campaigns, a difference the report expresses as 384 percent.

That comparison echoes the structure of DoubleVerify's own Q1 2026 quarterly benchmarks report , which similarly found fraud and SIVT violations falling 24 percent year over year to 0.5 percent globally in that earlier dataset, alongside a rising out-of-geo violation rate that ran counter to the broader trend.

In North America, the Fraud/SIVT Violation Rate on desktop stood at 0.9 percent, against 0.8 percent on mobile app and 0.5 percent on mobile web; desktop showed the steepest year-over-year reduction, at 48 percent.

In EMEA, the pattern reversed: mobile app recorded the largest improvement, falling 51 percent to reach a 0.4 percent violation rate, while desktop, at 0.8 percent, improved by 44 percent and mobile web, at 0.2 percent, improved by 49 percent.

The lab found that in unprotected media, AI bots generated 15 percent of clicks across the campaigns studied, and that in some individual studies, a monitored ad click was ten times more likely to come from a bot than from a human.

A State of Click Fraud Report published by Lunio in July 2026 found that 75.6 percent of surveyed marketers estimated losing more than 5 percent of their monthly performance budget to invalid traffic, while only 5.3 percent used a dedicated prevention platform.

North America's Brand Suitability Violation Rate fell to 4.1 percent, a 10 percent year-over-year reduction and the lowest of any region DoubleVerify tracks; the figure has now declined for three consecutive years, from 5.4 percent in 2023 to 4.6 percent in 2024 and 4.1 percent in 2025.

Within North America, the United States recorded a 4 percent violation rate against Canada's 8 percent, though Canada's figure dropped 11 percent year over year compared with a 9 percent reduction in the United States.
EMEA's rate fell only 2 percent, to 6.9 percent, and the region continued to underperform the 4.8 percent global benchmark.

The regional average obscured wide variation by market: France's violation rate dropped sharply, to 4 percent, below the global benchmark, while rates in Italy and Turkey rose year over year, and Eastern Europe recorded the highest subregional rate at 9.9 percent, even as that figure itself fell 14 percent from the prior year.
Globally, unprotected campaigns recorded a 13.8 percent brand suitability violation rate against 4.8 percent for protected campaigns, a gap DoubleVerify expresses as 189 percent.

The report's Vodafone Germany case study found that after implementing DoubleVerify's Authentic Brand Suitability product, the telecommunications company reduced media waste by 79 percent and its block rate by 72 percent, alongside CPM and quality-adjusted CPM reductions of 4 percent and 10 percent respectively.

Similar deployment findings for Vodafone in EMEA news environments appeared in an earlier PPC Land report from July 2025, which found the company had reduced block rates by 41 percent and keyword violations by 48 percent year over year, redirecting the resulting savings into additional purchases of news publisher inventory.
DoubleVerify says its AI SlopStopper tool blocked or monitored more than 500 million impressions across both regions in the first half of 2026 combined.

North American marketers reported far greater reluctance than their global counterparts about using AI to build ad copy and creatives: 63 percent said they were somewhat to very concerned, against a 48 percent global figure.
EMEA marketers showed the opposite pattern, expressing less concern than the global average, at 43 percent against 45 percent globally.

North American marketers proved the most wary of any group in either report about serving ads inside AI platforms, with 63 percent describing themselves as somewhat to very concerned, against a 50 percent global average; EMEA marketers were closer to that global figure, at 47 percent.

Consumer reactions in North America followed a similar pattern, with only the single scenario of "the ad is highly relevant to the chat" producing more positive than negative sentiment, at 31 percent positive against 19 percent negative.
Ads appearing alongside chats the report characterizes as negative or sad drew 34 percent negative sentiment in North America, the least favorable result recorded for any chat scenario tested.
North American marketers ranked transparent reporting on where ads are served and reliable measurement and attribution of ad performance as their top two requirements, both at 39 percent.
EMEA marketers instead prioritized the ability to review or approve AI-generated creatives, at 38 percent, ahead of data-privacy safeguards.

North America's overall viewable rate rose 4 percent year over year; video viewability in the United States specifically climbed 10 percent to reach 88 percent, while Canada's video rate rose a more modest 4 percent to 84 percent.

EMEA video viewability rose only 1 percent regionally, to 84 percent, still trailing the 87 percent global benchmark, though France recorded the sharpest single-market improvement in display viewability, up 8 percent to 67 percent.

July 19, 2025 - IAS identifies AI-generated slop sites as a major ad quality threat , finding quality inventory delivers 91 percent higher conversion rates.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Azure Annual Revenue Surpasses $100 Billion Mark for First Time: Microsoft Temporarily Clarifies AI Business Financials

According to the financial report, Microsoft's revenue in the fourth fiscal quarter reached 90 billion U.S. dollars, up 18% from 76.4 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, and 17% growth in constant currency, which exceeded the general expectation of 87.62 billion U.S. dollars from analysts surveyed by the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG).

Operating profit was 40.6 billion U.S. dollars, up 18% from 34.4 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, keeping pace with the revenue growth rate, indicating no dilution of the profitability of core businesses.
Net profit was 35.8 billion U.S. dollars, compared with 27.2 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, representing a year-on-year increase of 31%.
LSEG analysts generally expected 4.24 U.S. dollars in diluted EPS and 31.5 billion U.S. dollars in net profit, meaning the actual performance fully beat market expectations.

The company recorded a 3.2 billion U.S. dollar gain from its investment in Anthropic, and expenses related to the voluntary separation program were lower than the forward guidance previously provided by the company on April 29, 2026, which was partially offset by severance pay and impairment charges in the Xbox division.

Excluding the impact of the OpenAI investment, on a Non-GAAP basis, Microsoft's net profit was 35.3 billion U.S. dollars, up 22% from 28.8 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year; diluted earnings per share was 4.74 U.S. dollars, up 23% year-on-year.

The difference between GAAP and Non-GAAP in the fourth fiscal quarter was a net loss of 480 million U.S. dollars caused by the OpenAI investment, while the investment generated a net gain of 1.575 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, with a net impact change of 2.055 billion U.S. dollars.

For the full fiscal year 2026, Microsoft's total revenue reached 331.8 billion U.S. dollars, up 18% year-on-year, and 16% growth in constant currency; operating profit was 155.2 billion U.S. dollars, up 21% year-on-year, and 19% growth in constant currency; net profit was 133.7 billion U.S. dollars, up 31% year-on-year; diluted earnings per share was 17.95 U.S. dollars, up 32% year-on-year.
In the fourth fiscal quarter, Microsoft returned 10.2 billion U.S. dollars to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

01 Azure's annual revenue exceeds 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time Financial performance of Microsoft's three major business segments Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud division generated revenue of 39.3 billion U.S. dollars in the fourth fiscal quarter, compared with about 29.9 billion U.S. dollars in the same period last year, representing a year-on-year increase of 32% and 31% growth in constant currency, exceeding the general expectation of 38.16 billion U.S. dollars from analysts surveyed by StreetAccount.

Revenue from Azure and other cloud services increased by 43% this quarter, compared with a 40% growth rate in the previous quarter, accelerating by 3 percentage points, marking the fastest quarterly growth rate since the beginning of 2022.

This performance significantly exceeded Microsoft's previous guidance range of 39% to 40% in constant currency, and was also higher than the 39.6% expected by analysts surveyed by CNBC and StreetAccount.
The actual 43% growth rate directly eliminated this risk.
Satya Nadella, Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, disclosed in the financial report that Azure's full-year revenue for fiscal 2026 exceeded 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time.

Azure's 43% growth rate at its current volume means an annual increment of more than 40 billion U.S. dollars, and its absolute growth value is equivalent to the total revenue of some mid-sized cloud vendors.
Microsoft's remaining commercial performance obligations reached 6.78 trillion U.S. dollars at the end of the fourth fiscal quarter, up 84% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter.

Microsoft disclosed in January 2026 that about 45% of its then 6.25 trillion U.S. dollars of remaining commercial performance obligations were related to OpenAI, and the growth of commitments from non-OpenAI customers this quarter is diluting this concentration.

The overall revenue of Microsoft's cloud business in the fourth fiscal quarter was 59.3 billion U.S. dollars, up 27% year-on-year, covering Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial cloud, Dynamics 365, LinkedIn and other commercial cloud services.

Amy Hood, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Microsoft, said in the financial report: "We closed the fiscal year with strong performance, highlighted by Microsoft Cloud revenue of 59.3 billion U.S. dollars, up 27% year-on-year."

Microsoft's Productivity and Business Processes division recorded revenue of 37.8 billion U.S. dollars in the fourth fiscal quarter, up 14% year-on-year, exceeding the general expectation of 37.19 billion U.S. dollars from analysts surveyed by StreetAccount.
The number of paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30 million.
Three months ago, Microsoft disclosed that this figure was about 20 million, representing a quarter-on-quarter increase of about 50%.
Brad Reback, an analyst at Stifel, previously predicted that this number would be 26 million, and the actual figure far exceeded expectations.
Revenue from Microsoft 365 commercial cloud increased by 14% on a reported basis, and 16% after adjustment.
Revenue from Microsoft 365 consumer cloud increased by 24%, and 22% in constant currency, showing that cloud service subscriptions on the individual user side also maintain robust growth.
Revenue from LinkedIn increased by 12%, and 10% in constant currency.
Revenue from Dynamics 365 increased by 13%, and 12% in constant currency, with stable demand for enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management software.

This year, Azure's revenue exceeded 100 billion U.S. dollars for the first time, and the number of paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats surpassed 30 million, which reflects customers' trust in our ability to help them with AI transformation."
